title: Hackensack Meridian Health earns first Joint Commission AI certification in U.S.
text:
Hackensack Meridian Health earns first Joint Commission AI certification in U.S.
S. M. Holmes
Hackensack Meridian Health became the first health network in the United States to earn the Joint Commission’s Responsible Use of AI in Healthcare Certification, according to an Aug. 5 announcement. The certification recognizes Hackensack Meridian Health for establishing governance, safeguards, monitoring, and education systems to ensure responsible use of artificial intelligence across its operations.
The Joint Commission is an independent nonprofit organization that accredits and certifies hospitals and other healthcare organizations nationwide. Its Responsible Use of AI in Healthcare (RUAIH) Certification is a voluntary program focused on encouraging ethical adoption of artificial intelligence throughout clinical care and operational processes.
“At Hackensack Meridian Health, we are committed to integrating AI responsibly and safely across our health network to advance the way we deliver care,” said Robert C. Garrett, FACHE, CEO of Hackensack Meridian Health. “AI has the potential to help clinicians detect diseases earlier, personalize treatment for every patient, improve the efficiency of our hospitals, and reduce administrative work that contributes to burnout,” Garrett said. “Most importantly, it enables physicians, nurses and team members to spend more time caring for patients.”
Hackensack Meridian Health operates 18 hospitals and over 500 patient care locations statewide as New Jersey’s largest health network. The company outlined that it has built a comprehensive framework guided by formal AI governance structures combining data security with ongoing evaluation and monitoring of AI tools. This includes role-specific training as well as general literacy programs so staff can confidently explain how artificial intelligence supports patient care.
Joel Klein, M.D., executive vice president and chief digital and information officer at Hackensack Meridian Health, said: “The promise of artificial intelligence is not to replace the human side of medicine, but to strengthen it. We’re leveraging this technology to give our providers time to focus on what matters most – the patients they serve.”
Ken Grubbs, DNP, MBA, RN—chief nursing executive at the Joint Commission—said: "AI continues to rapidly transform the healthcare industry, helping healthcare organizations improve clinical decision-making, enhance operational efficiency, reduce administrative burden, and support patient care." Grubbs continued: "Organizations must ensure the use of AI is guided by strong governance, rigorous oversight, and an unwavering focus on patient safety. Joint Commission commends HMH for demonstrating a responsible approach to AI adoption while advancing innovation in patient care."
The New Jersey Business and Industry Association serves private-sector employers throughout New Jersey; it advances competitive excellence among its members through advocacy efforts while facilitating partnerships between businesses, government entities, and academic institutions, according to the official website.
